# Poste Italiane (PST.MI) — a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-07-21 for the investment committee. Quote listing: Milan (Borsa Italiana), euros; live price EUR 27.51 (verified intraday 2026-07-21; prior close EUR 27.59). Sources: six quarterly earnings calls (Q2 2024 through Q3 2025), the screener trajectory, and live-verified 2026 public facts.*

**One-line frame:** Poste Italiane is not a postal company — it is a state-controlled financial-services, insurance and payments platform with a mail-and-parcel network attached. Management is candid and has repeatedly out-delivered its own guidance; precisely because of that, the stock has re-rated about 28% this year alone to a 52-week-high region (EUR 17.49–29.48 range) and now trades above the analyst consensus target of roughly EUR 23.5. The forensic question is not "is management lying" (they are not) but "is anything left in the price" — asked three days before a new multi-year plan (July 24, 2026) and mid-way through a EUR 10.8 billion exchange offer to swallow Telecom Italia outright.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Across the six calls the story is unusually stable: the "platform company" — one retail relationship with Italians (26.5 million daily interactions; a Super App that reached 15 million users by late 2025) cross-sold across four engines: Mail/Parcel, Financial Services (BancoPosta), Insurance (Poste Vita) and Postepay (payments, telco, energy).

- **Q2 2024:** operational — a four-year national labor contract signed "in record time," fixing the cost base through 2027 and enabling a parcel-dedicated delivery network; full-year operating profit guidance upgraded to EUR 2.8 billion.
- **Q3 2024:** record net interest income (NII — the spread earned on deposits and the government-bond book) takes center stage; interim dividend up 39%.
- **Q1 2025:** the story expands from execution to empire — the purchase of Vivendi's 15% of TIM takes the stake to 24.8%, framed as consolidating the Italian telco market, with a mobile-network contract already signed.
- **Q2 2025:** another guidance raise (operating profit to EUR 3.2 billion). Management volunteers a regime change: 2025 is "a turning year" — from 2026, portfolio capital gains must begin substituting for fading NII.
- **Q3 2025:** the ten-year listing anniversary — record everything, Super App migration complete, TIM synergies contracted (TIM Energia live in 750 shops, an MVNO migration saving EUR 20 million a year, a cloud joint venture), record interim dividend up 21%.
- **Live 2026 (verified):** the narrative's logical endpoint — on March 22, 2026 Poste launched a voluntary cash-and-shares tender offer for all of TIM (~EUR 10.8 billion; EUR 1.67 cash plus 0.218 new Poste shares per 10 TIM shares, ~EUR 0.635 per TIM share, a ~9% premium to March 20; validity conditional on 66.67% acceptance, delisting intended). Consob approved the offer document July 16; the acceptance window runs July 20 to September 11, 2026, payment September 18. Poste pegs the cash outlay at roughly EUR 2.8 billion at full take-up and claims ~EUR 700 million of annual pre-tax synergies (~EUR 500 million cost).

What was quietly de-emphasized: mail. The CEO refused false comfort in Q3 2024 — that side of the business "is bound to suffer going forward" — and by 2025 mail is purely a repricing story. Nothing material was dropped; energy retail (~950,000 clients), protection insurance and the TIM program were added and have so far shown up in the numbers.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

A caution on the screener block first: several fields are artifacts of consolidating a bank-and-insurer inside an industrials template. The revenue series (EUR 31.6B in 2021 "collapsing" to EUR 13.5B in 2024, then "surging" to EUR 21B) reflects insurance-accounting presentation (IFRS 17 grossing/netting), not the business; the ~1% return on invested capital and the 0.0 solvency score are meaningless for a deposit-and-float balance sheet; and the recomputed EUR 57.5 billion of borrowings-minus-cash is overwhelmingly BancoPosta/Poste Vita customer funding, not corporate leverage. The reliable spine is earnings and the company's own segment disclosures.

| Management claim | The numbers | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Record EBIT, raised guidance" (every call) | Adjusted operating profit ~EUR 2.8B (2024) → EUR 3.2B (2025, delivered on record EUR 13.1B revenue) → 2026 guided above EUR 3.3B in February, raised to ~EUR 3.4B on May 7 after a record Q1 (revenue EUR 3.5B +8%, operating profit EUR 905M +14%) | **Matches — and then some.** Three straight years of raise-then-deliver |
| "Record net profit" | EUR 1.99B (2024) → EUR 2.21B (2025) → 2026 guided EUR 2.3B excluding TIM; trailing-twelve-month diluted EPS EUR 1.88, latest quarter +37% | **Matches** |
| Parcel share gains "in all customer segments" | Volumes +23–26% (2024), +9–14% (2025) vs a market growing high single digits | **Matches** — though average tariffs fall on mix; profitable but low-margin |
| Mail decline "effectively mitigated through repricing" | Volumes fall mid-to-high single digits; revenue held roughly flat by tariff increases | **Half-true and candid about it** — repricing is a finite lever, and management says so |
| Cost discipline | Labor fixed through 2027; net margin ~10.5%; the screener flags margins 1.26 standard deviations ABOVE the historical peak | **Matches, with a warning:** the earnings base a buyer pays ~15x for is a peak base |

Where the story is **richer than the numbers justify:** the TIM takeover. It is pitched as synergy-rich, but it is paid partly in newly printed Poste shares — at full acceptance TIM's outside shareholders would own on the order of a fifth of the enlarged company — a large, dilutive, judgment-heavy swing into a structurally challenged telco, dressed as platform strategy. The market has treated it as an overhang, and the offer's own arithmetic (issuing ~15x-earnings paper for a ~6x-cash-flow telco plus EUR 700M of claimed synergies) is accretive only if integration goes to plan.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rising, from already-high — no defensive drift.** Q2 2024: "accelerating our strong, profitable and cash-generative growth." Q2 2025: "another record-breaking quarter." Q3 2025: decennial triumphalism. Guidance language grew MORE specific over time (the CFO volunteers basis-point portfolio-yield detail), and the two real risks — mail decline and the NII fade — are raised unprompted by management itself, which is a credibility marker. The risk at this point is not evasion; it is hubris at the top of a rate cycle.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**High — the strongest single fact in the file.** 2024: lifted to EUR 2.8B, hit. 2025: lifted to EUR 3.2B (net EUR 2.2B), hit. 2026: opened above EUR 3.3B, lifted to ~EUR 3.4B in May. NII guidance in 2024 was beaten through the top of the raised range. The dividend marched with it: EUR 1.08/share for 2024; EUR 1.6B total for 2025 (+16%); policy floor above 70% of net profit excluding TIM, TIM dividends passed through cash-for-cash; the EUR 0.85 final was paid in June 2026. The screener's 71% beat rate (5 of 7) understates an annual raise-then-deliver machine. The flip side: a market that has learned the pattern pre-pays for the raise — which is what a 52-week-high multiple means.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **NII durability** — "top of everybody's agenda" (the CEO's own words, Q2 24). Pressed every quarter; the honest terminal answer is that 2025 was the turning year and capital gains (EUR 1.9B unrealized by mid-2025) must fill the gap. This is the most-pressed, least-resolved line.
- **The TIM logic** — Berenberg's "where is the benefit of that stake?" drew the candid admission that it is equity-accounted, gives no solvency benefit, and costs ~EUR 40M of foregone NII; the value case rests on synergies and future TIM dividends.
- **Headcount and labor cost** — full-time employees rising toward 120,000 against a plan that implied restraint; answered as growth-driven and pay-for-performance; confirms operating leverage is limited.
- **The CDP agreement** (the state lender whose postal savings Poste distributes for EUR 1.6–1.9 billion a year in fees, roughly EUR 1.7B expected for 2026): the current contract dies December 31, 2026, deliberately sequenced around the spring 2026 mandate season. Management gives process answers, not economics — a quiet single-counterparty dependency the market is not pricing.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- 🔴 **Peak-cycle earnings mix** (Q2 25 admission): the NII engine behind the 2023–25 profit surge is rolling over; the substitute — discretionary bond capital gains — is lower-quality earnings.
- 🔴 **The EUR 10.8B TIM takeover**: large, partly stock-funded, dilutive, into a structurally challenged telco; acceptance window open now (July 20–September 11, 2026). The single biggest capital-allocation judgment risk in the story.
- 🔴 **Margins 1.26 sigma above their historical peak** and the stock 84% up its 52-week range, +20% above its 200-day average — the easy money is behind it.
- 🔴 **Zero insider buying** through a +28% year-to-date run.
- 🔴 **CDP renewal cliff**: EUR ~1.7B of high-margin fees reprice against a state counterparty by December 31, 2026. Precedent favors renewal; economics can still tighten.
- 🟢 **Three years of raised-and-delivered guidance**; labor costs contractually fixed to end-2027.
- 🟢 **Sticky franchise**: EUR 600B+ total financial assets; retail deposits stable at EUR 58B; insurance lapse rate below the industry's, much of it deliberate rebalancing.
- 🟢 **Fortress capital**: insurance Solvency II ratio 312% (Q3 25) versus a ~200% ambition.
- 🟢 **Governance overhang resolved**: the Treasury renewed CEO Del Fante for a fourth three-year term and the new board confirmed him on April 27, 2026.
- 🟢 **TIM synergies partly contracted, not conceptual**: the EUR 20M/year MVNO saving is signed; energy distribution is live; the 24.8% stake is marked around EUR 1.9B versus EUR 1.1B invested.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

Three tells. First, the vocabulary pivot from "NII" to "capital gains" and "synergies" as forward value drivers — an implicit admission that the rate tailwind that drove the re-rating is turning, and that growth now leans on the harder-to-underwrite TIM integration. Second, the dividend framing shifted to an explicitly *competitive* posture — "we look at our peer group… in the banking sector, including the buyback programs" (Q3 25) — a team managing its shareholder base around a stretched valuation, and telegraphing which multiple set (banks and insurers, at ~10x earnings) it wants to be judged against, an uncomfortable comparison at ~15x. Third, the CDP contract was deliberately sequenced around the CEO-mandate question — management itself treated spring 2026 as an open governance question; that half of the overhang has since resolved in continuity's favor, leaving the CDP half live.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STRENGTHENING operationally — but the price already knows.** This is a high-quality, well-run, state-backed compounder whose management has earned trust. The problem is entirely price and timing, not quality.

The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: **the buyer today pays roughly 15 times trailing earnings — a decade-high multiple, above the street's EUR ~23.5 consensus target — at the precise moment the dominant profit engine is, by management's own account, peaking; while management deploys ~EUR 10.8 billion of partly newly printed stock to swallow a telco (result known by September 11–18, 2026, with a share-flowback wave if it succeeds); with a EUR ~1.7B/year state fee contract expiring December 31, 2026; and with a new multi-year plan landing July 24, 2026 — inside the densest macro-event week of the year — that must validate expectations the market has already pre-paid.**

**Economic moat: NARROW and STABLE.** Real but bounded advantages — a regulatory-license and physical-distribution moat (the unmatched national branch network, the CDP postal-savings franchise, sticky low-cost deposits, state ownership, the largest Italian consumer app). Return on equity (~16.5%) is solid and steady rather than rising; gross margin is contracting on parcel mix. Not eroding on the evidence, but its cash value hangs partly on two negotiated state contracts rather than pure market power.

**Secular threat: manageable, not terminal.** Mail is in structural decline but is a small slice of profit with a repricing offset; payments disintermediation is the theoretical long-run tail, yet Postepay is gaining transaction share, not losing it. No structural force credibly impairs the terminal earnings base. The screener's deep-value tag is therefore a mis-tag: this is neither a fear-print nor a value trap — it is a fully-valued quality name after the re-rating, with a peak-earnings artifact flattering the optics.

# Poste Italiane (PST.MI) — a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-07-21 for the investment committee. Quote listing: Milan (Borsa Italiana), euros; live price EUR 27.51 (verified intraday 2026-07-21; prior close EUR 27.59). Sources: six quarterly earnings calls (Q2 2024 through Q3 2025), the screener trajectory, and live-verified 2026 public facts.*

**One-line frame:** Poste Italiane is not a postal company — it is a state-controlled financial-services, insurance and payments platform with a mail-and-parcel network attached. Management is candid and has repeatedly out-delivered its own guidance; precisely because of that, the stock has re-rated about 28% this year alone to a 52-week-high region (EUR 17.49–29.48 range) and now trades above the analyst consensus target of roughly EUR 23.5. The forensic question is not "is management lying" (they are not) but "is anything left in the price" — asked three days before a new multi-year plan (July 24, 2026) and mid-way through a EUR 10.8 billion exchange offer to swallow Telecom Italia outright.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Across the six calls the story is unusually stable: the "platform company" — one retail relationship with Italians (26.5 million daily interactions; a Super App that reached 15 million users by late 2025) cross-sold across four engines: Mail/Parcel, Financial Services (BancoPosta), Insurance (Poste Vita) and Postepay (payments, telco, energy).

- **Q2 2024:** operational — a four-year national labor contract signed "in record time," fixing the cost base through 2027 and enabling a parcel-dedicated delivery network; full-year operating profit guidance upgraded to EUR 2.8 billion.
- **Q3 2024:** record net interest income (NII — the spread earned on deposits and the government-bond book) takes center stage; interim dividend up 39%.
- **Q1 2025:** the story expands from execution to empire — the purchase of Vivendi's 15% of TIM takes the stake to 24.8%, framed as consolidating the Italian telco market, with a mobile-network contract already signed.
- **Q2 2025:** another guidance raise (operating profit to EUR 3.2 billion). Management volunteers a regime change: 2025 is "a turning year" — from 2026, portfolio capital gains must begin substituting for fading NII.
- **Q3 2025:** the ten-year listing anniversary — record everything, Super App migration complete, TIM synergies contracted (TIM Energia live in 750 shops, an MVNO migration saving EUR 20 million a year, a cloud joint venture), record interim dividend up 21%.
- **Live 2026 (verified):** the narrative's logical endpoint — on March 22, 2026 Poste launched a voluntary cash-and-shares tender offer for all of TIM (~EUR 10.8 billion; EUR 1.67 cash plus 0.218 new Poste shares per 10 TIM shares, ~EUR 0.635 per TIM share, a ~9% premium to March 20; validity conditional on 66.67% acceptance, delisting intended). Consob approved the offer document July 16; the acceptance window runs July 20 to September 11, 2026, payment September 18. Poste pegs the cash outlay at roughly EUR 2.8 billion at full take-up and claims ~EUR 700 million of annual pre-tax synergies (~EUR 500 million cost).

What was quietly de-emphasized: mail. The CEO refused false comfort in Q3 2024 — that side of the business "is bound to suffer going forward" — and by 2025 mail is purely a repricing story. Nothing material was dropped; energy retail (~950,000 clients), protection insurance and the TIM program were added and have so far shown up in the numbers.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

A caution on the screener block first: several fields are artifacts of consolidating a bank-and-insurer inside an industrials template. The revenue series (EUR 31.6B in 2021 "collapsing" to EUR 13.5B in 2024, then "surging" to EUR 21B) reflects insurance-accounting presentation (IFRS 17 grossing/netting), not the business; the ~1% return on invested capital and the 0.0 solvency score are meaningless for a deposit-and-float balance sheet; and the recomputed EUR 57.5 billion of borrowings-minus-cash is overwhelmingly BancoPosta/Poste Vita customer funding, not corporate leverage. The reliable spine is earnings and the company's own segment disclosures.

| Management claim | The numbers | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Record EBIT, raised guidance" (every call) | Adjusted operating profit ~EUR 2.8B (2024) → EUR 3.2B (2025, delivered on record EUR 13.1B revenue) → 2026 guided above EUR 3.3B in February, raised to ~EUR 3.4B on May 7 after a record Q1 (revenue EUR 3.5B +8%, operating profit EUR 905M +14%) | **Matches — and then some.** Three straight years of raise-then-deliver |
| "Record net profit" | EUR 1.99B (2024) → EUR 2.21B (2025) → 2026 guided EUR 2.3B excluding TIM; trailing-twelve-month diluted EPS EUR 1.88, latest quarter +37% | **Matches** |
| Parcel share gains "in all customer segments" | Volumes +23–26% (2024), +9–14% (2025) vs a market growing high single digits | **Matches** — though average tariffs fall on mix; profitable but low-margin |
| Mail decline "effectively mitigated through repricing" | Volumes fall mid-to-high single digits; revenue held roughly flat by tariff increases | **Half-true and candid about it** — repricing is a finite lever, and management says so |
| Cost discipline | Labor fixed through 2027; net margin ~10.5%; the screener flags margins 1.26 standard deviations ABOVE the historical peak | **Matches, with a warning:** the earnings base a buyer pays ~15x for is a peak base |

Where the story is **richer than the numbers justify:** the TIM takeover. It is pitched as synergy-rich, but it is paid partly in newly printed Poste shares — at full acceptance TIM's outside shareholders would own on the order of a fifth of the enlarged company — a large, dilutive, judgment-heavy swing into a structurally challenged telco, dressed as platform strategy. The market has treated it as an overhang, and the offer's own arithmetic (issuing ~15x-earnings paper for a ~6x-cash-flow telco plus EUR 700M of claimed synergies) is accretive only if integration goes to plan.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Rising, from already-high — no defensive drift.** Q2 2024: "accelerating our strong, profitable and cash-generative growth." Q2 2025: "another record-breaking quarter." Q3 2025: decennial triumphalism. Guidance language grew MORE specific over time (the CFO volunteers basis-point portfolio-yield detail), and the two real risks — mail decline and the NII fade — are raised unprompted by management itself, which is a credibility marker. The risk at this point is not evasion; it is hubris at the top of a rate cycle.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**High — the strongest single fact in the file.** 2024: lifted to EUR 2.8B, hit. 2025: lifted to EUR 3.2B (net EUR 2.2B), hit. 2026: opened above EUR 3.3B, lifted to ~EUR 3.4B in May. The screener's 71% beat rate (5 of 7) understates an annual raise-then-deliver machine. The flip side: a market that has learned the pattern pre-pays for the raise — which is what a 52-week-high multiple means.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **NII durability** — "top of everybody's agenda" (the CEO's own words, Q2 24). Pressed every quarter; the honest terminal answer is that 2025 was the turning year and capital gains (EUR 1.9B unrealized by mid-2025) must fill the gap. This is the most-pressed, least-resolved line.
- **The TIM logic** — Berenberg's "where is the benefit of that stake?" drew the candid admission that it is equity-accounted, gives no solvency benefit, and costs ~EUR 40M of foregone NII; the value case rests on synergies and future TIM dividends.
- **Headcount and labor cost** — full-time employees rising toward 120,000 against a plan that implied restraint; answered as growth-driven and pay-for-performance; confirms operating leverage is limited.
- **The CDP agreement** (the state lender whose postal savings Poste distributes for EUR 1.6–1.9 billion a year in fees, roughly EUR 1.7B expected for 2026): the current contract dies December 31, 2026, deliberately sequenced around the spring 2026 mandate season. Management gives process answers, not economics — a quiet single-counterparty dependency the market is not pricing.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

- 🔴 **Peak-cycle earnings mix** (Q2 25 admission): the NII engine behind the 2023–25 profit surge is rolling over; the substitute — discretionary bond capital gains — is lower-quality earnings.
- 🔴 **The EUR 10.8B TIM takeover**: large, partly stock-funded, dilutive, into a structurally challenged telco; acceptance window open now (July 20–September 11, 2026). The single biggest capital-allocation judgment risk in the story.
- 🔴 **Margins 1.26 sigma above their historical peak** and the stock 84% up its 52-week range, +20% above its 200-day average — the easy money is behind it.
- 🔴 **Zero insider buying** through a +28% year-to-date run.
- 🔴 **CDP renewal cliff**: EUR ~1.7B of high-margin fees reprice against a state counterparty by December 31, 2026. Precedent favors renewal; economics can still tighten.
- 🟢 **Three years of raised-and-delivered guidance**; labor costs contractually fixed to end-2027.
- 🟢 **Sticky franchise**: EUR 600B+ total financial assets; retail deposits stable at EUR 58B; insurance lapse rate below the industry's, much of it deliberate rebalancing.
- 🟢 **Fortress capital**: insurance Solvency II ratio 312% (Q3 25) versus a ~200% ambition.
- 🟢 **Governance overhang resolved**: the Treasury renewed CEO Del Fante for a fourth three-year term and the new board confirmed him on April 27, 2026.
- 🟢 **TIM synergies partly contracted, not conceptual**: the EUR 20M/year MVNO saving is signed; energy distribution is live; the 24.8% stake is marked around EUR 1.9B versus EUR 1.1B invested.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

Three tells. First, the vocabulary pivot from "NII" to "capital gains" and "synergies" as forward value drivers — an implicit admission that the rate tailwind that drove the re-rating is turning, and that growth now leans on the harder-to-underwrite TIM integration. Second, the dividend framing shifted to an explicitly *competitive* posture — "we look at our peer group… in the banking sector, including the buyback programs" (Q3 25) — a team managing its shareholder base around a stretched valuation, and telegraphing which multiple set (banks and insurers, at ~10x earnings) it wants to be judged against, an uncomfortable comparison at ~15x. Third, the CDP contract was deliberately sequenced around the CEO-mandate question — management itself treated spring 2026 as an open governance question; that half of the overhang has since resolved in continuity's favor, leaving the CDP half live.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Trajectory: STRENGTHENING operationally — but the price already knows.** This is a high-quality, well-run, state-backed compounder whose management has earned trust. The problem is entirely price and timing, not quality.

The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: **the buyer today pays roughly 15 times trailing earnings — a decade-high multiple, above the street's EUR ~23.5 consensus target — at the precise moment the dominant profit engine is, by management's own account, peaking; while management deploys ~EUR 10.8 billion of partly newly printed stock to swallow a telco (result known by September 11–18, 2026, with a share-flowback wave if it succeeds); with a EUR ~1.7B/year state fee contract expiring December 31, 2026; and with a new multi-year plan landing July 24, 2026 — inside the densest macro-event week of the year — that must validate expectations the market has already pre-paid.**

**Economic moat: NARROW and STABLE.** Real but bounded advantages — a regulatory-license and physical-distribution moat (the unmatched national branch network, the CDP postal-savings franchise, sticky low-cost deposits, state ownership, the largest Italian consumer app). Return on equity (~16.5%) is solid and steady rather than rising; gross margin is contracting on parcel mix. Not eroding on the evidence, but its cash value hangs partly on two negotiated state contracts rather than pure market power.

**Secular threat: manageable, not terminal.** Mail is in structural decline but is a small slice of profit with a repricing offset; payments disintermediation is the theoretical long-run tail, yet Postepay is gaining transaction share, not losing it. No structural force credibly impairs the terminal earnings base. The screener's deep-value tag is therefore a mis-tag: this is neither a fear-print nor a value trap — it is a fully-valued quality name after the re-rating, with a peak-earnings artifact flattering the optics.

# Poste Italiane (PST.MI) — Forensic Dossier

*Continuing coverage. Prior committee verdict 2026-07-27: pass for now, conviction 2. This update refreshes the evidence against six quarters of calls (Nov-2024 through the 2026-07-24 first-half call) and the live tape at EUR 26.21.*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story management tells has been remarkably consistent, and that consistency is itself the headline. From the very first call in this window (nine-month 2024) to the latest (first-half 2026), Poste describes itself as a "platform company" — a single trusted relationship with the Italian household, monetised across mail and parcels, banking, insurance and payments. The through-line never wavers: "record" results, "relentless cost discipline," market-share gains in low-margin volume businesses, and a fortress balance sheet.

What has evolved is the emphasis. In late 2024 the growth engine was net interest income (the money earned on the government-bond portfolio funded by postal deposits), riding the high-rate environment — "the highest nine months NII recorded since listing" (Q3-24). By mid-2025 management began openly flagging that this was a peak: "you could probably consider 2025 as a turning year, and from 2026 is probably going to be a different pattern" (Q2-25), pointing to capital gains on the bond book replacing NII as rates fall. By 2026 the narrative has pivoted forward to three self-help levers that do not depend on rates: (1) the TIM (Telecom Italia) acquisition and its synergies, (2) a "financial hub" reorganisation collapsing four business units into two to free up bank capital and cut headcount, and (3) a hub-and-spoke redesign of the 13,000-office physical network. The new CDP postal-savings distribution agreement for 2027-2030 (term sheet agreed, +~EUR 100M of revenue) was added in July 2026 to shore up visibility on the one financial-services revenue stream investors most feared was at risk.

Growth drivers quietly de-emphasised: mail volume (management stopped pretending it can stabilise) and prepaid-card stock counts (falling on the end of government welfare cards, reframed toward transaction value and market share).

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | The numbers | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Record" revenue and profit "every quarter" | Net income marches up cleanly: EUR 1.58B (2021) → 1.58B (2022) → 1.92B (2023) → 1.99B (2024) → 2.21B (2025); TTM diluted EPS 1.88, latest-quarter EPS +37% YoY | Corroborated — on the metric that matters (net income), not the headline revenue |
| Strong "revenue growth" | The scan shows revenue swinging 31.6B → 13.5B → 21.05B across 2021-25 and "+56% YoY" | A red herring — these swings are an insurance-accounting artifact (gross vs. net premium presentation under IFRS 17), NOT operating volatility. The screener's "deep value / +56% growth" tag is built on this noise |
| Raised-and-delivered guidance | FY-2024 EBIT guided to EUR 2.8B and delivered; FY-2025 guidance was RAISED mid-year (Q2-25) to EUR 3.2B EBIT / EUR 2.2B net profit and then confirmed; screener logs a 71% earnings-beat rate (5 of 7 quarters) | Corroborated — a genuine raise-then-deliver record |
| "Fortress" balance sheet | Insurance Solvency II ratio ~303-315% across the period, far above the ~200% ambition; ROE 16.5% | Corroborated |
| Low returns / "deep value" screen | ROIC 1.0%, Altman-Z 0.0, net-debt figures in the tens of billions | Misleading as stated — for a balance sheet dominated by a bank (BancoPosta) and an insurer (Poste Vita), "borrowings" are the funding base of the banking operation, not corporate leverage, and ROIC/Altman-Z are near-meaningless. ROE (16.5%) is the honest return metric |

The core finding: the company is a steady mid-single-digit compounder wearing a deep-value costume sewn from conglomerate and insurance-accounting artifacts. The story is neither richer nor poorer than the trajectory — it is accurately told; the screener mis-reads it.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable-to-rising, and unusually candid.** Each call opens with "record" and "resilience," but management repeatedly volunteers its own bad news rather than being cornered into it. On mail: "unfortunately, I don't think we can call it structural... that side of the business is bound to suffer going forward" (Q3-24). On NII: "2025 as a turning year... from 2026 is probably going to be a different pattern" (Q2-25). The language is offensive (platform, cross-sell, market share, super-app conversion rates) rather than defensive; cost discipline is framed as a competitive weapon, not a survival measure. Guidance specificity increased over the window (segment-level EBIT bridges, CSM growth rates, Solvency walk-throughs).

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**High.** The clearest test: the FY-2025 guide was lifted mid-year to EUR 3.2B EBIT / EUR 2.2B net profit (Q2-25) and reconfirmed at nine months and again in the FY-2026 first-half call — no walk-back. FY-2024 landed on its EUR 2.8B EBIT / EUR 2B net-profit target. The 71% beat rate corroborates a modest, deliverable-guidance culture with no evidence of aggressive sandbagging or of stretch targets that later slipped. Reliability: High.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Analysts (Berenberg's Huttner most persistently) circled three worries, and management addressed each head-on: (1) *Can mail really be flat?* — answered honestly "no." (2) *Is NII sustainable?* — answered "no, it peaks, capital gains take over." (3) *Why is the TIM stake worth it and where does the value show up?* — management walked through the EUR 20M/year MVNO saving, energy cross-sell, the JV, and the equity-accounted (not marked-to-market) treatment. The one recurring soft spot is quantification of the newer self-help levers: the financial-hub cross-sell and capital-release upside is repeatedly described as "tens of millions" of NII plus unquantified cross-sell — real but not yet sized, and not landing until 2027. No topic was deflected into later bad news within this window.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
